summary.headline: SRG Housing Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 50% YoY to INR 9 crore; FY26 AUM crossed INR 1,000 crore at INR 1,042 crore, up 37%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 net interest income of about INR 28 crore (up 33% YoY) and NIM of 11.28%, with PAT of about INR 9 crore (up 50%). For FY26, NII was INR 98.26 crore (up 31%), PAT INR 32.49 crore (up 33%), and disbursements INR 443.54 crore (up 45%). Asset quality was stable, with GNPA at 1.77% and NNPA at 0.65%, and the company was upgraded to A- Stable by Acuité. Management guided to FY27 disbursements of about INR 600 crore and AUM of INR 1,400 to 1,500 crore, and flagged a possible equity raise later in the year.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: About 94% of the loan book is from rural and semi-urban markets; Rajasthan and Gujarat together make up about 77% of AUM per an individual investor's calculation, which management did not dispute. Operations span six states and one union territory with 96 branches. Expansion is focused on the southern states (Tamil Nadu, Telangana) with 10 to 15 new branches planned by year-end.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: About 79% of customers are self-employed (one analyst cited about 75% of the loan book). Around 97% of EMI collections come through the banking channel, and cash collections are 4% to 5%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target of about INR 600 crore (per CEO), against INR 443.54 crore in FY26.
AUM expected at INR 1,300 to 1,400 crore, with an INR 1,500 crore stretch target by the end of FY27.
Cost of borrowing expected to fall from 10.88% to about 10.70% over the next one to two years. The call initially cited 63% to 61%, which was corrected by a company note.
ROE guidance of 12% to 13%, with a longer-term aim of about 18% per management, depending on the housing market.
Two-year AUM target of about INR 2,000 crore, and INR 2,000 to 2,500 crore within two and a half to three years. Long-term vision of INR 10,000 to 20,000 crore.
Equity raise considered in Q4 FY27 if the year progresses well; otherwise in Q1 or Q2 FY28, once leverage crosses 5x to 6x (bank comfort level, versus 12x NHB limit).
capex_capacity: Branch expansion of 10 to 15 new branches in Tamil Nadu and Telangana by end of FY27; no new branches planned in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan or MP.
Target AUM per branch of about INR 25 crore, implying about INR 110 crore per branch at scale (management target, not a stated timeline).
Ongoing ERP overhaul and digital transformation (SRG SRAJAN); AI-based calling in development, with no cost incurred yet per management. IT headcount increased.
Capital adequacy of 38.62% gives headroom for growth, but leverage is expected to rise toward the 5x to 6x bank comfort limit as AUM grows.
demand_pricing: Average ticket size rose 41% YoY to INR 15.44 lakh in Q4, which management attributed to higher land and construction costs and changing customer aspirations rather than a shift in customer profile.
Average LTV rose to about 50.7% from about 46.6% a year earlier; management said this reflects product nature, not a deliberate strategy.
Management said there is no meaningful competitive pressure from larger lenders on pricing, as the customer profile is unchanged.
Management said the West Asia conflict and weaker monsoon are not materially affecting the book, citing diversified, small-ticket self-employed borrowers.

qa_highlights.question: Would the new branches' scale-up and the INR 500 crore disbursement guidance hold for the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Disbursement target was raised to about INR 600 crore for FY27; AUM expected at INR 1,300 to 1,400 crore, with INR 1,500 crore as the stretch. New branches focus on Tamil Nadu and Telangana (10 to 15 branches).

qa_highlights.question: How will the rating upgrade affect cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects borrowing cost to decline; the call's 63% to 61% figure was a transcription error. The corrected expectation is a fall from 10.88% to about 10.70% over one to two years, with no firm guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: What ROE is the company targeting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 12% to 13% for the coming period, with about 18% over time as the housing market improves.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA high in Rajasthan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no specific cause; Rajasthan is the largest state by portfolio size, so its share of GNPA is higher, and no concern was seen in the state.

qa_highlights.question: Is capitalisation adequate for AUM growth, and how is equity being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding access has widened after the upgrade (banks, equity markets, NCDs). Leverage can reach 12x under NHB rules, but banks cap it at 5x to 6x, so equity may be raised in Q4 FY27 or Q1/Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Stage 1 about 93% of the book, and how does collection work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Stage 1 is 93.05%, Stage 2 5.18% and Stage 3 1.77%. About 14% to 15% of cheques bounce, about 90% of which are recovered within the month, and around 97% of amounts are recovered within 30 days of a bounce.

risks_watch: Rajasthan GNPA trend: the company said portfolio size, not credit issues, explains the figure, but the state remains a large share of AUM.
Equity dilution timing: raise is planned for Q4 FY27 or Q1/Q2 FY28 depending on leverage, which would affect ROE and EPS.
Execution of the southern expansion (10 to 15 branches) and new management hires, which could raise costs and cost of borrowing in the near term.
Concentration: Rajasthan and Gujarat together account for about 77% of AUM per an investor calculation; management expects this to even out over two to three years.
Ticket size and LTV drift: average LTV rose from about 46.6% to 50.7% and ticket size rose 41%, so the credit profile needs monitoring.
Management's 12% to 13% ROE guidance is below the 18% longer-term aim, and the CEO was uncertain about borrowing cost guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, funding access and asset quality, with a clear FY27 target. Less precise on specifics: the CEO declined to guarantee borrowing-cost numbers, and the call had transcription errors on cost of borrowing that were corrected in a company note. Answers on the Rajasthan GNPA and the collection structure were defensive and relied on process explanations.
key_quotes: Our AUM was INR 26 crore in FY'14, which has increased to INR 1042 crore in FY'26.
Around 97% of our collections come through banking channels, and the majority of our repayments are received through this route.
Basically, it is not a strategy and there is no risk profile to it.
